reconstructed_theorem_text: E_n=EuclideanSpace R (Fin(n+1)), the real (n+1)-coordinate space with its l2 Euclidean norm. Let S_n={z in E_n: ||z||=1}, considered as a subtype when it is used as a carrier. For a function a:S_n -> A into a type with a distinguished zero, write R(a)(z)=0 if z=0 and R(a)(z)=a(z/||z||) otherwise; normalization is the first component of the supplied H. For a:S_n->R and x:S_n, let Q(a,x)=P_(x-perp)(gradient_R R(a)(x)), where P_(x-perp) is starProjection onto the orthogonal complement of the real span of x. The supplied projection formulas make this b-<x,b>x for b=gradient_R R(a)(x). Here gradient_R h(x) is exactly the inverse Riesz map applied to fderiv_R h x. For every scalar function a on S_n and point x in S_n, the target defines Q(a,x) by exactly this formula. There is no differentiability assumption: gradient and fderiv remain their total Lean operators. The projection is confirmed by the supplied unit-vector identities, but this definition does not itself prove an actual derivative exists or identify Q with a separately defined intrinsic Riemannian gradient.
objects: An arbitrary a:S_n->R, unit point x and a projected ambient vector.
quantifiers: Implicit n; then a and x.
assumptions: No smoothness, differentiability or integrability premise; unit norm is carried by x:S_n.
conclusion: Defined vector: starProjection onto (R x)^perp of gradient_R R(a)(x).
scopes: Pointwise evaluation at a unit vector. Literal total derivative operator; no existence/regularity theorem is added.
constant_dependencies: Unit-normal projection b -> b-<x,b>x, with coefficient 1 and no scaling by dimension.
